transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-03 15:00 PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Ava Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood CSM); Laura Kim (Meridian Head of ML), Raj Singh (Infra), Emily Turner (Security)

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll keep this tight, 30-40 minutes. quick check - everyone see the eval sheet I dropped in the drive?
[00:12] Laura: yeah I pulled it up, looks like overall accuracy held, but there's a regression on the fraud-detection prompts, especially the multi-turn clarifications.
[00:23] Ava: right, so we saw precision drop from 0.88 to 0.74 on that subset when we applied the aggressive temperature and top-k settings for diversity. some of that looks like prompt ambiguity - model is hallucinating extra entities.
[00:38] Raj: can you remind me which model variant this was running on? the staging cluster is hitting the quantized 8-bit build?
[00:46] Ava: yeah this run was on rwd-v2-quant8, it's the one we recommended for cost parity. note: the KV cash (KV cache) warmup wasn't fully exercised which might explain some context misses.
[00:58] Emily: quick security note - we need to make sure the eval logs are stored in our S3 bucket and not sent to any third party. also, SOC2 artifact still outstanding from your team.
[01:10] Samir: absolutely, we'll share the SOC 2 report and the KMS/HSM integration doc after this.
[01:18] Laura: ok, on the regression, can you walk through the examples you flagged? I saw about 22 failing prompts with false positives.
[01:28] Ava: sure, example one - prompt about unusual transaction phrasing - model added a suspicious merchant that wasn't in the input. that's a hallucination likely triggered by the open-ended follow-up probe in the prompt. I'm proposing we tighten the guardrail by adding an explicit "only use entities present in the input" instruction and a negative example set.
[01:45] Samir: and to be clear, that's a soft guardrail; we can also implement a post-filter that rejects entity additions unless confidence > 0.85 or model votes agree.
[01:56] Laura: votes? you mean ensembling across variants?
[02:00] Ava: yeah, simple ensemble or fallback to a smaller deterministic model for entity extraction. cost tradeoff though.
[02:06] Raj: speaking of cost - our infra budget is tight. what does Dedicated look like cost-wise versus hosted? we need estimates for monthly commit.
[02:15] Samir: I'll send a pricing note. ballpark: Dedicated will be higher fixed cost but lower per-token at scale. for the pilot size you're running (~10M tokens/month estimate), Dedicated becomes favorable if latency SLOs are strict.
[02:29] Emily: we care about data residency too; logs must stay in our AWS account. can Redwood support private deployment or VPC peering?
[02:37] Samir: yes, Private can be deployed into your VPC; we support KMS integration and HSM for key material. details in the doc I'll share.
[02:47] Laura: back to prompts - Ava, you mentioned new negative cases, what's the plan for v2?
[02:53] Ava: v2 will add ~150 negative examples and a clarified instruction block. we'll also add a scoring rubric: pass / soft-fail / fail, with thresholds based on exact-match and semantic similarity (sentence-bert style). we'll include comments explaining why each example failed.
[03:10] Laura: can the scoring be reproducible? we need to show product owners the delta week-over-week.
[03:16] Ava: yes - we'll export the eval CSV with columns: prompt_id, expected, model_output, score_numeric, score_label, notes. we'll put a version tag on the prompt set.
[03:25] Priya: adding that we'll link the eval to the monitoring dashboard so any regression alert triggers a channel notification.
[03:31] Raj: about latency - we want p95 under 200ms for single-turn extraction flows. what does p95 look like on your staging Dedicated?
[03:39] Ava: on our staging last week p95 was ~240ms for the quant8 build at batch size 8. p50 was 85ms. p99 spikes depend on long-tail token counts. we can tune batching and KV cache warmup to improve p95.
[03:52] Raj: ok we'll run a 3-run test against your Dedicated staging and upload the numbers.
[03:57] Laura: also, when you changed temperature and top-k earlier, did you re-evaluate the confidence calibration? the model seemed overconfident on hallucinations.
[04:05] Ava: good point - calibration shifted. we can add a calibration pass using Platt scaling on the logits based on a holdout set. that'll help thresholds.
[04:15] Emily: one more security ops note - audit logs need to be immutable and have export controls for compliance. is that supported?
[04:22] Samir: yes, audit logs are configurable for retention and can be pushed to your S3 with object locking. I'll attach the doc.
[04:30] Laura: great. on evaluation results, are there specific categories where regression is concentrated?
[04:36] Ava: mainly multi-turn clarifications and entity resolution where the prompt allowed open-ended generation. single-turn, deterministic extraction held up well. we suspect the interaction between temperature and the new system tokenization patch caused it.
[04:48] Raj: tokenization patch? did I miss a release note?
[04:51] Ava: it's an internal change to limit subword splits to reduce decode overhead; it slightly changed logits on fringe tokens. we'll mark it in the release notes; it may affect edge-case phrasing.
[05:03] Laura: can we rollback that for a narrow cohort if needed?
[05:06] Samir: yes, we can route traffic to the previous model variant for a canary window. Redwood supports rollouts and automatic fallback policies.
[05:15] Laura: perfect. next, for guardrails - we prefer a layered approach: prompt constraints, post-filter, and model voting. what does Redwood recommend as default?
[05:23] Ava: start with tightened prompts + negative examples, then a confidence thresholding post-filter. if still risky, fallback to a smaller extraction model or route to human review.
[05:33] Laura: human-in-the-loop isn't ideal for scale; can we prioritize reducing false positives to <2%?
[05:39] Ava: that's achievable with the new prompt set and calibration; we'll validate in v2.
[05:45] Priya: action-wise, Ava will deliver prompt v2 and scoring rubric; Samir will send pricing and security docs; Raj will run latency tests; Laura will share anonymized logs.
[05:56] Samir: any blockers or open risks we should log?
[06:00] Emily: main blocker is SOC2 evidence for Private deployment and confirmation on KMS/HSM integration patterns. also need confirmation that audit logs are immutable in your current offering.
[06:10] Samir: noted - will attach SOC2 and KMS doc.
[06:13] Laura: timeline wise - if we get v2 prompts and run tests this week, can we reconvene next Monday?
[06:19] Samir: next Monday works, 6/09 same time?
[06:22] Laura: yes.
[06:24] Samir: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the sheet and docs.
[06:28] Priya: thanks all, bye.

Notes: transcription contains minor errors ("KV cash" etc.). References to shared artifacts: eval CSV (link provided in meeting chat), Dedicated staging benchmarking sheet (internal link), SOC2 and KMS docs to be shared via secure link.

End of transcript.
